regions.name: Latissimus dorsi
regions.description: The broad lats extend and draw the arm toward your body. Pull-ups, pulldowns, and rows all involve this muscle.

exercises.name: Pull-up
exercises.instructions: Begin in a controlled hang. Draw your elbows down and pull your chest toward the bar. Lower without dropping. Use assistance if needed.
exercises.cue: Keep the movement controlled instead of kicking for momentum.
exercises.alsoWorks: Biceps, brachialis, forearm flexors; rhomboids and trapezius assist

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
exercises.instructions: Sit securely and pull the bar toward your upper chest. Return overhead with control.
exercises.cue: Keep the bar in front of your head and avoid excessive backward lean.

regions.name: Rhomboids
regions.description: These deeper muscles retract the shoulder blades and support controlled rowing movements.

exercises.name: Chest-supported row
exercises.instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench. Pull the dumbbells toward your ribs, then lower to a comfortable stretch.
exercises.cue: Let your shoulder blades move without lifting your chest.
exercises.alsoWorks: Middle trapezius, latissimus dorsi, posterior deltoids, biceps

exercises.name: Reverse fly
exercises.instructions: Hinge at the hips or support your chest on a bench. Open the arms outward with a slight elbow bend. Return slowly.
exercises.cue: Keep your neck relaxed and the load light enough to control.

regions.name: Erector spinae
regions.description: A group running along the spine that extends the trunk and resists forward bending.
regions.note: The spinal extensors mainly resist movement in these exercises.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
exercises.instructions: With soft knees, push your hips back and keep the bar near your legs. Stop when you reach your controlled hinge depth, then stand.
exercises.cue: Move at the hips while maintaining a steady back position.
exercises.alsoWorks: Hamstrings, gluteus maximus; forearms maintain grip

exercises.name: Bird dog
exercises.instructions: Start on hands and knees. Extend the opposite arm and leg without rotating your trunk, pause, then return and switch sides.
exercises.cue: Reach long rather than lifting high.

regions.name: Upper trapezius
regions.description: The upper fibers elevate the shoulder blade and contribute to its upward rotation. Shrugs load the elevation action.

exercises.name: Dumbbell shrug
exercises.instructions: Stand with dumbbells at your sides. Raise your shoulders toward your ears, pause briefly, and lower with control.
exercises.cue: Keep your head neutral; avoid rolling your shoulders.

exercises.name: Farmer carry
exercises.instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and walk with short, controlled steps. Keep your torso upright and the weights steady.
exercises.cue: Use a load that allows a neutral wrist and steady posture.
exercises.alsoWorks: Forearm flexors, abdominal wall; lower body supports the carry

regions.name: Middle trapezius
regions.description: These fibers retract the shoulder blade toward the spine and contribute to controlled rows.

exercises.name: Chest-supported row
exercises.instructions: Support your chest on an incline bench and row toward your ribs. Allow controlled shoulder-blade movement as you lower.
exercises.cue: Keep your chest supported. The lats and other back muscles also work.
exercises.alsoWorks: Rhomboids, posterior deltoids, latissimus dorsi, biceps

exercises.name: Reverse fly
exercises.instructions: Hinge at the hips or support your chest on a bench. Open the arms outward with a slight elbow bend. Return slowly.
exercises.cue: Keep your neck relaxed and the load light enough to control.

regions.name: Lower trapezius
regions.description: The lower fibers help depress and upwardly rotate the shoulder blade, working with other shoulder-girdle muscles.

exercises.name: Prone Y raise
exercises.instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench. With thumbs upward, lift your arms into a Y through a comfortable range. Lower slowly.
exercises.cue: Start with bodyweight or very light weights and avoid arching your back.
exercises.alsoWorks: Middle and upper trapezius, serratus anterior; rotator cuff stabilizes
